    da=sum(dp)/len(dp); db=sum(dst)/len(dst)
    ratio = db/da if da else float('inf')
    print(f"{label:8s} {ta:9.2f} {tb:9.2f} {tb-ta:7.2f} {da:9.3f} {db:9.3f} {db-da:7.3f}  {ratio:10.2f}")

# Check if F3_Z01 damper is pegged at max or not (post-July)
dsp_values_post = [v for t,v in data[ids['F3_Z01_dmsp']] if t >= '2018-07-01']
dsp_values_pre  = [v for t,v in data[ids['F3_Z01_dmsp']] if t <  '2018-07-01']
print(f"\nF3_Z01 damper pre:  mean={sum(dsp_values_pre)/len(dsp_values_pre):.3f}, max={max(dsp_values_pre):.3f}, %>0.5 = {100*sum(1 for v in dsp_values_pre if v>0.5)/len(dsp_values_pre):.1f}%")
print(f"F3_Z01 damper post: mean={sum(dsp_values_post)/len(dsp_values_post):.3f}, max={max(dsp_values_post):.3f}, %>0.5 = {100*sum(1 for v in dsp_values_post if v>0.5)/len(dsp_values_post):.1f}%")

content.text: Data supports local load change. F3_Z01's temperature rose (~2°C) along with a large increase in damper setpoint (0.19→0.44, max 0.82, ~45% of hours above 0.5). If the zone sensor were reading high, the controller would think the zone is warm and reduce the cooling damper — but instead the damper is going up, indicating genuine thermal demand. The other zones also rose (seasonal effect), but F3_Z01's damper response is the strongest, consistent with a local load increase.
